p: The Chew Valley is one of the prettiest bits of countryside within reach of Bristol, a patchwork of farmland, stone villages and two big reservoirs, Chew Valley Lake and Blagdon Lake, tucked beneath the northern edge of the Mendip Hills. It's easy to combine any animal visit here with a proper countryside day.

Chew Valley Lake is a favourite with birdwatchers, and there are waterside paths and picnic spots near the main parking areas. Blagdon Lake, just to the west, is quieter and known for fly fishing. Nearby, the village of Stanton Drew is home to a set of prehistoric stone circles, among the largest in the country, and they sit in a field you can simply wander into, which kids find delightfully strange.

Villages such as Chew Magna have pubs and tearooms for lunch, and the Mendip Hills just south are an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty with hill walks and views over Somerset. A car is the easiest way to get around, as buses through the valley are limited. Smaller animal parks can change their opening days through the year, so do look up the latest details before setting off.
